l: rest of the Lord their God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 13
s: The high priesthood is taught so that people may enter into the rest of the Lord. Those who are made pure and spotless before God enter into that rest.

l: ordinances, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 13
s: The ordinances of the holy order were given as a type of the Son's order. They were intended to help people look forward to the Son for a remission of their sins and entry into the rest of the Lord.

l: glad tidings, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 13
s: Glad tidings of great joy are declared by angels to all nations and to people scattered across the earth. They prepare hearts to receive the word at the time of the Son's coming.

l: day of salvation, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 13
s: Alma declares that the day of salvation is drawing near and calls on the people to repent.

l: coming of Christ, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 13
s: The coming of the Son will be declared by angels to just and holy men, fulfilling the words of the fathers. Alma waits for and rejoices in this coming, whether it occurs sooner or later.

l: eternal life, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 13
s: People are urged to have hope that they will receive eternal life and to have the love of God in their hearts so they may be lifted up at the last day.

l: The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 14
s: Alma and Amulek are bound, imprisoned, mocked, deprived, and questioned after testifying against the wickedness of the people. Zeezrom repents and pleads for them, while believers, women and children, and the holy scriptures are cast into a fire. The Lord permits the innocent to die, but later gives Alma and Amulek strength according to their faith in Christ, enabling them to break their bonds. The prison collapses, killing the chief judge, lawyers, priests, teachers, and every soul inside except Alma and Amulek, and the people flee in fear.

l: Alma, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 14
s: Alma is bound with strong cords, imprisoned, beaten, mocked, deprived of food, water, and clothing, and questioned by the chief judge and others. He refuses to answer them, then cries to the Lord for strength according to his faith in Christ; he breaks his bonds and survives the collapse of the prison.

l: Amulek, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 14
s: Amulek is bound, imprisoned, beaten, mocked, and deprived of food, water, and clothing with Alma. He asks Alma to save the women and children from the flames, then breaks his bonds through the power granted according to faith in Christ and survives the prison's collapse.

l: Zeezrom, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 14
s: Zeezrom becomes astonished and harrowed by consciousness of his guilt after recognizing the blindness caused by his lying words. He declares Alma and Amulek spotless before God and pleads for them, but the people revile him, spit upon him, and cast him out.

l: Lord, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 14
s: The Lord receives those consumed by the fire up to himself in glory and permits the people to act according to the hardness of their hearts. He does not allow Alma and Amulek to be burned because their work is not finished, and he grants them power according to their faith in Christ.

l: God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 14
s: God is testified to as one, with a Son who should come among the people. The chief judge falsely argues that God did not save those cast into the fire because they were of Alma and Amulek's faith.

l: people, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 14
s: Many people believe Alma's words and begin to repent and search the scriptures, but the greater part seeks to destroy Alma and Amulek. They testify against them, cast out believers, burn believers and records, abuse Alma and Amulek, and flee in fear when the prison collapses.

l: wives and children of the expelled believers, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 14
s: The women and children who believe or have been taught to believe in the word of God are brought together and cast into the fire. Amulek is pained when he sees them consuming in the flames, but Alma says the Spirit constrains him not to save them.

l: land of Ammonihah, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 14
s: The chief judge over the land of Ammonihah comes to the prison on the twelfth day of the tenth month in the tenth year of the reign of the judges, accompanied by teachers and lawyers.

l: prison, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 14
s: Alma and Amulek are confined in the prison for many days while being bound, mocked, beaten, and deprived. The walls are rent in twain and fall to the earth after Alma and Amulek break their cords.

l: fire, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 14
s: The fire consumes the women, children, and other believers who are cast into it, as well as the records containing the holy scriptures.

l: holy scriptures, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 14
s: The people bring forth records containing the holy scriptures and cast them into the fire so that they may be burned and destroyed.

l: law, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 14
s: The people accuse Alma and Amulek of reviling the law, and they are mocked for judging the people and condemning the law.

l: word of God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 14
s: Those who believe or have been taught to believe in the word of God are cast out and sent to be stoned or burned.

l: faith of Christ, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 14
s: The faith of Alma and Amulek is associated with the power that allows them to break their bonds and survive the prison's collapse.

l: miraculous power of God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 14
s: The power of God comes upon Alma and Amulek after the chief judge and others have finished smiting them. It enables them to rise, stand, break their cords, and come out of the fallen prison unharmed.

l: judgment, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 14
s: Alma says the deaths of the innocent will stand as a witness and cry against the people at the last day, making the Lord's judgments against them just.

l: martyrdom, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 14
s: Alma and Amulek are carried to the place of martyrdom to witness the destruction of those consumed by fire.

l: martyrdom of the believers, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 14
s: The people burn believing women and children and others who believe or have been taught to believe in the word of God. Alma and Amulek witness the destruction, and Alma says the Lord permits it according to the hardness of the people's hearts.

l: imprisonment of Alma and Amulek, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 14
s: Alma and Amulek are bound with strong cords and imprisoned for many days. They are questioned, beaten, mocked, deprived of food, water, and clothing, and finally break their bonds through the power of God.

l: collapse of the prison, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 14
s: The earth shakes mightily and the prison walls are rent in twain and fall to the earth. The chief judge, lawyers, priests, teachers, and every soul within the walls except Alma and Amulek are slain, while Alma and Amulek come forth unharmed.

l: The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 15
s: Alma and Amulek departed from Ammonihah and came to the land of Sidom, where they found people cast out for believing Alma. Zeezrom, sick with a burning fever because of his sins and anguish, was healed after affirming his belief in Christ and Alma prayed for him. Alma baptized Zeezrom, who then preached, and Alma established a church in Sidom where many people were baptized. The people of Ammonihah remained hard-hearted, while the people in Sidom humbled themselves, worshipped, and prayed.

l: Alma, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 15
s: Alma departed with Amulek for the land of Sidom and found people who had been cast out of Ammonihah. He asked Zeezrom whether he believed in the power of Christ unto salvation, prayed for his healing, baptized him, established a church in Sidom, and later took Amulek to Zarahemla.

l: Amulek, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 15
s: Amulek departed with Alma for Sidom and had forsaken his gold, silver, and precious things in Ammonihah for the word of God. Alma later took him to his own house in Zarahemla and administered to him in his tribulations.

l: Zeezrom, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 15
s: Zeezrom lay sick in Sidom with a burning fever caused by the tribulations of his mind and his sins. He believed Alma's words about Christ's redemption, was healed after Alma prayed, was baptized, and began preaching to the people.

l: land of Sidom, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 15
s: The land of Sidom was where Alma and Amulek found people who had departed from Ammonihah. Zeezrom was healed there, Alma established a church there, and many people from the surrounding region were baptized.

l: land of Ammonihah, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 15
s: The land of Ammonihah was the place from which people were cast out and where Amulek left his gold, silver, and precious things. Its remaining people continued in hard-heartedness and did not repent.

l: people who had departed out of the land of Ammonihah, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 15
s: These people had been cast out and stoned because they believed in the words of Alma. They told Alma and Amulek what had happened to their wives, children, and themselves.

l: people of Sidom, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 15
s: The people of Sidom were astonished when Zeezrom was healed, and knowledge of the healing spread throughout the land. Many people from the surrounding region were baptized after Alma established a church there.

l: people of Ammonihah, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 15
s: The people of Ammonihah remained hard-hearted and stiff-necked and did not repent of their sins. They attributed Alma and Amulek's power to the devil and did not believe in repentance.

l: power of Christ unto salvation, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 15
s: Alma asked Zeezrom whether he believed in the power of Christ unto salvation. Zeezrom affirmed his belief.

l: Christ, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 15
s: Zeezrom believed in Christ and in the words Alma had taught. His healing occurred according to his faith in Christ.

l: redemption of Christ, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 15
s: Alma taught that if Zeezrom believed in the redemption of Christ, he could be healed. Zeezrom said that he believed according to Alma's words.

l: healing of Zeezrom, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 15
s: The healing of Zeezrom occurred after Alma prayed to the Lord for mercy and asked that Zeezrom be healed according to his faith in Christ. Zeezrom leaped to his feet and walked, astonishing the people.

l: Lord, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 15
s: Alma cried unto the Lord to have mercy on Zeezrom and heal him according to his faith in Christ.

l: God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 15
s: The people in Sidom assembled at their sanctuaries to worship God before the altar. They watched and prayed continually to be delivered from Satan, death, and destruction.

l: baptism of Zeezrom, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 15
s: Alma baptized Zeezrom unto the Lord after Zeezrom was healed. Zeezrom began preaching to the people from that time forth.

l: church in the land of Sidom, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 15
s: Alma established a church in the land of Sidom and consecrated priests and teachers to baptize those who desired baptism.

l: baptism of the people of Sidom, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 15
s: Many people from the region around Sidom were baptized after the church was established there.

l: repentance, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 15
s: The people of Ammonihah did not repent of their sins and did not believe in repentance of their sins.

l: humbling of the people of Sidom, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 15
s: The people in Sidom began to humble themselves before God after a great check as to the pride of their hearts. They assembled at their sanctuaries to worship God and watched and prayed continually.

l: The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 16
s: The Lamanites invaded Ammonihah and surrounding areas, destroying the city and taking captives before Zoram and his sons led the Nephite armies to recover them. Alma received revelation that the Lamanites would cross the river Sidon in the south wilderness, where they would be defeated and the captives returned. Ammonihah was left desolate, and its dead were associated with the Desolation of Nehors. Alma, Amulek, and other priests preached repentance, the word of God, the coming and resurrection of the Son of God, and the church became established throughout the land amid peace and spiritual blessings.

l: people of Nephi, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 16
s: The people of Nephi experienced an invasion, followed by three years of continual peace throughout the land. The church became generally established among them, and the Lord poured out his Spirit to prepare them to receive the word of God.

l: Nephites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 16
s: The Nephites raised armies against the invading Lamanites and recovered their captive brethren. They later enjoyed peace and received preaching throughout the land.

l: Lamanites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 16
s: The Lamanites invaded the borders of the land, destroyed Ammonihah, killed people around Noah, and took others captive. They were later scattered and driven into the wilderness by the Nephite armies.

l: Zarahemla, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 16
s: Zarahemla had experienced much peace before a cry of war was heard throughout the land.

l: land of Ammonihah, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 16
s: Ammonihah was invaded and destroyed by the Lamanites. Its land remained desolate for many years because of the dead bodies and their scent.

l: people of Ammonihah, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 16
s: The people of Ammonihah were destroyed by the Lamanites, and every living soul of them was killed.

l: Ammonihahites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 16
s: The Ammonihahites were destroyed, and their great city was left desolate in one day.

l: armies of the Lamanites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 16
s: The armies of the Lamanites entered through the wilderness, destroyed Ammonihah, and took captives. They were met, scattered, and driven into the wilderness by the Nephite armies.

l: Nephite armies, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 16
s: The Nephite armies crossed the river Sidon and marched into the south wilderness under Zoram and his sons. They defeated the Lamanites and recovered every captive without losing any of them.

l: war, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 16
s: After many years without wars or contentions, a cry of war was heard when the Lamanites invaded the land. The Lamanites did not come again to war against the Nephites until the fourteenth year of the reign of the judges.

l: peace, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 16
s: There had been much peace in the land before the invasion. After the Lamanites were driven out, the people of Nephi had continual peace for three years.

l: captives, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 16
s: The Lamanites took people captive into the wilderness. Zoram and his sons recovered the captives, and not one of them was lost.

l: Zoram, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 16
s: Zoram was appointed chief captain over the armies of the Nephites. With his sons Lehi and Aha, he asked Alma where to search for the captives and led the armies to recover them.

l: Lehi, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 16
s: Lehi was one of Zoram's two sons and helped lead the Nephite armies in searching for and recovering the captives.

l: Aha, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 16
s: Aha was one of Zoram's two sons and helped lead the Nephite armies in searching for and recovering the captives.

l: Alma, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 16
s: Alma was high priest over the church and was believed to have the spirit of prophecy. He inquired of the Lord, directed Zoram where to find the Lamanites, and preached repentance and the word of God.

l: Amulek, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 16
s: Amulek went with Alma preaching repentance and the word of God in temples, sanctuaries, and synagogues.

l: Lord, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 16
s: The Lord revealed through Alma where the Lamanites would be met and where the captives would be delivered. The Lord poured out his Spirit on the land to prepare people to receive the word.

l: God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 16
s: God was taught as the one whose rest people could enter by receiving the word. The Son of God was taught to come after his resurrection.

l: river Sidon, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 16
s: The river Sidon was the place the Lamanites would cross in the south wilderness. Zoram and his sons crossed it and met the Lamanite armies on its east side.

l: Desolation of Nehors, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 16
s: The land of Ammonihah was called the Desolation of Nehors because the slain people belonged to the profession of Nehor. The land remained desolate after the destruction.

l: church, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 16
s: The church became generally established throughout the land among the people of the Nephites. Its preaching was accompanied by the Lord's blessings and the absence of inequality.

l: priests, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 16
s: The priests preached against lying, deceiving, envy, strife, malice, reviling, stealing, robbing, plundering, murdering, adultery, and lasciviousness. They also taught the coming, sufferings, death, and resurrection of the Son of God.

l: word of God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 16
s: Alma, Amulek, and others preached the word of God throughout the land without respect of persons. The people were prepared to receive it with joy and enter into the rest of the Lord their God.

l: Son of God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 16
s: The priests taught the coming, sufferings, and death of the Son of God. They taught that he would appear to the people after his resurrection.

l: resurrection of the dead, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 16
s: The resurrection of the dead was taught as part of the preaching about the Son of God. The people heard that the Son of God would appear after his resurrection.

l: repentance, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 16
s: Alma, Amulek, and many others preached repentance throughout the land.

l: coming of Christ, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 16
s: The coming of the Son of God was taught as an event that would shortly come. The people were taught that he would appear to them after his resurrection.

l: The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 17
s: Alma meets the sons of Mosiah and rejoices that they remain strong in the knowledge of the truth after fourteen years of teaching among the Lamanites. The sons of Mosiah recount their journey from the land of Zarahemla, their afflictions, and the Lord’s command to establish his word among the Lamanites. Ammon becomes a servant of king Lamoni in the land of Ishmael and is assigned to watch Lamoni’s flocks. When Lamanites scatter the flocks at the water of Sebus, Ammon defends them with his sling and sword and returns the flocks to the king.

l: Alma, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 17
s: Alma meets the sons of Mosiah while journeying from the land of Gideon toward the land of Manti. He rejoices because they remain his brethren in the Lord and have grown strong in the knowledge of the truth.

l: sons of Mosiah, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 17
s: The sons of Mosiah have searched the scriptures, prayed, fasted, and taught with power and authority of God. They refused the kingdom, departed from the land of Zarahemla, and spent fourteen years teaching among the Lamanites despite many afflictions.

l: Lord, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 17
s: The Lord visits the sons of Mosiah and those with them with his Spirit, comforts them, and commands them to establish his word among the Lamanites. He promises to make them instruments unto the salvation of many souls.

l: God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 17
s: God gives the sons of Mosiah the word and power to teach among the Lamanites. The people are brought before the altar of God to call on his name and confess their sins.

l: Lamanites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 17
s: The Lamanites are described as wild, hardened, ferocious, indolent, and inclined to murder, rob, and plunder Nephites. The sons of Mosiah go among them to teach the word of God and bring them, if possible, to repentance and knowledge of the plan of redemption.

l: land of Zarahemla, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 17
s: The sons of Mosiah depart from the land of Zarahemla after refusing the kingdom their father desired to confer upon them.

l: land of Ishmael, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 17
s: Ammon enters the land of Ishmael, where the Lamanites bind him and carry him before king Lamoni. Ammon becomes a servant there and watches the king’s flocks.

l: the waters of Sebus, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 17
s: The water of Sebus is the place where the Lamanitish servants take the flocks to drink. Lamanites scatter the flocks there, and Ammon confronts them at the waters.

l: Lamoni, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 17
s: King Lamoni rules the land of Ishmael and is a descendant of Ishmael. He is pleased with Ammon, frees him, offers him one of his daughters to wife, and then appoints him among the servants who watch his flocks.

l: Ammon, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 17
s: Ammon goes to the land of Ishmael, chooses to be king Lamoni’s servant, and watches the king’s flocks. When the flocks are scattered, he gathers them, kills some attackers with his sling, cuts off the arms of those who strike at him, and brings the severed arms as testimony before the king.

l: Lamanitish servants, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 17
s: The Lamanitish servants work with Ammon to drive Lamoni’s flocks to the water of Sebus. They fear the king will slay them after the flocks are scattered, but they follow Ammon’s instructions and help encircle and recover the flocks.

l: the king’s flocks, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 17
s: The flocks of Lamoni are driven to the water of Sebus and scattered by certain Lamanites. Ammon and the servants gather them again, protect them, water them, and return them to the king’s pasture.

l: slings, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 17
s: Ammon uses his sling with mighty power to cast stones at the Lamanites who scatter the flocks. He kills six of them with the sling.

l: arms, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 17
s: Ammon smites off the arms of the men who lift clubs against him. The severed arms are carried before king Lamoni as testimony of what the attackers did.

l: holy scriptures, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 17
s: The sons of Mosiah search the scriptures diligently so that they may know the word of God.

l: word of God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 17
s: The sons of Mosiah teach the word of God among the Lamanites. The Lord commands them to establish his word, and Ammon teaches and directs the servants while defending the flocks.

l: truth, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 17
s: The sons of Mosiah grow strong in the knowledge of the truth and bring many Lamanites to that knowledge through their teaching.

l: the tradition of the Lamanites' fathers, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 17
s: The sons of Mosiah seek to bring the Lamanites to understand the baseness of the traditions of their fathers, which were not correct.

l: repentance, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 17
s: The sons of Mosiah undertake their work in hope of bringing the Lamanites to repentance. The promises of the Lord are extended to the Lamanites on the conditions of repentance.

l: redemption, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 17
s: The sons of Mosiah seek to bring the Lamanites to know the plan of redemption.

l: journey from Zarahemla to Nephi, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 17
s: The sons of Mosiah leave the land of Zarahemla with selected companions, weapons, and provisions for the wilderness. They journey to the land of Nephi, separate in the borders of the land of the Lamanites, and trust that they will meet again after their harvest.

l: teaching among the Lamanites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 17
s: The sons of Mosiah teach among the Lamanites for fourteen years. Their teaching has much success, and many are brought to the knowledge of the truth and before the altar of God.

l: conversion of the Lamanites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 17
s: The sons of Mosiah undertake their work to bring the Lamanites to repentance and to the knowledge of the truth and the plan of redemption. The text says that many are brought to the knowledge of the truth through their words.

l: Ammon becoming Lamoni's servant, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 17
s: Ammon declines king Lamoni’s offer to take one of his daughters to wife and says that he will be the king’s servant. He is then assigned to watch Lamoni’s flocks.

l: the scattering of the flocks, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 17
s: Certain Lamanites scatter the flocks of Ammon and the other servants at the water of Sebus. The servants fear that king Lamoni will kill them because the flocks have been scattered.

l: Ammon's defense of the flocks, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 17
s: Ammon tells the servants to encircle the flocks while he contends with the attackers. He kills some with stones, cuts off the arms of those who attack him with clubs, drives the attackers away, and restores the flocks to the king.

l: The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 18
s: King Lamoni’s servants testify that Ammon defended the king’s flocks and defeated those who attacked them, causing Lamoni to believe that Ammon is the Great Spirit. Ammon teaches Lamoni and his servants about God, the creation, the fall of man, their history, the scriptures, the plan of redemption, and the coming of Christ. Lamoni believes Ammon’s words, prays for mercy, and falls to the earth as if dead, after which his servants carry him to his wife.

l: Lamoni, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 18
s: King Lamoni learns from his servants about Ammon’s faithfulness and power and believes that Ammon is the Great Spirit. He asks Ammon about his power, believes his teachings about God and the plan of redemption, prays for mercy, and falls to the earth as if dead.

l: Ammon, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 18
s: Ammon defends king Lamoni’s servants and flocks, killing seven attackers with a sling and sword and cutting off the arms of others. He perceives Lamoni’s thoughts and teaches Lamoni and his servants about God, the scriptures, the plan of redemption, and the coming of Christ.

l: Lord, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 18
s: The Great Spirit is the tradition of king Lamoni and his people. Ammon teaches that the Great Spirit is God, who created all things, dwells in heaven with holy angels, knows the thoughts and intents of the heart, and created all people.

l: Lamanitish servants, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 18
s: King Lamoni’s servants testify about Ammon’s defense of the flocks and their own lives. They say that Ammon cannot be slain by the king’s enemies and that his strength and expertness make him a friend to the king.

l: Lamanites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 18
s: The Lamanites practice standing by the waters of Sebus to scatter people’s flocks and plunder those who are driven away. King Lamoni’s tradition includes belief in a Great Spirit, although they suppose that whatever they do is right.

l: the king’s flocks, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 18
s: The king’s flocks are scattered by Lamanites at the waters of Sebus. Ammon preserves the flocks and prevents the king’s enemies from scattering them while he is present.

l: the plan of redemption, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 18
s: The plan of redemption was prepared from the foundation of the world. Ammon expounds it to king Lamoni and his servants and teaches them about the coming of Christ and the works of the Lord.

l: The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 19
s: Ammon visits king Lamoni after Lamoni has lain as if dead for two days and tells the queen that he will rise. Lamoni awakens, declares that he has seen his Redeemer, and the queen, Ammon, and the servants are overcome by the Spirit and fall to the earth. Abish raises the queen and king, after which Lamoni, Ammon, and the servants teach the people, many of whom believe, are baptized, and establish a church. The work of the Lord begins among the Lamanites as the Lord pours out his Spirit upon them.

l: Ammon, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 19
s: Ammon goes to the queen and then sees king Lamoni, knowing that he is not dead. He teaches the queen, prays and gives thanks to God, is overcome with joy and falls to the earth, and later teaches the people.

l: Lamoni, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 19
s: King Lamoni lies on his bed for two days and two nights, then rises according to Ammon's words. He declares that he has seen his Redeemer, is overcome with joy, and later rebukes and teaches his people.

l: queen (wife of king Lamoni), The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 19
s: The queen sends for Ammon and asks him to see her husband. She believes Ammon's words, is blessed for her exceeding faith, falls under the power of the Spirit, and rises when Abish takes her by the hand.

l: Abish, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 19
s: Abish is a Lamanitish woman who had been converted to the Lord for many years because of a remarkable vision of her father. She remains standing when the others fall, gathers the people, and raises the queen and king.

l: Lamanites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 19
s: The Lamanites include Lamoni's people, among whom contention arises about Ammon and the events at the king's house. Many believe the teachings of Lamoni, Ammon, and the servants, are baptized, and become a righteous people.

l: Nephites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 19
s: The Nephites are the people among whom there had been mourning because of the Lamanites' iniquities and traditions. Ammon is identified as a Nephite, and some Lamanites say the Great Spirit had attended and delivered the Nephites.

l: Lamanitish servants, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 19
s: The servants testify to the king about Ammon's power, fall to the earth after calling on the name of the Lord, and later declare that their hearts had been changed and that they no longer desired to do evil.

l: the people, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 19
s: The people gather at the king's house, see the king, queen, servants, and Ammon lying on the earth, and contend about what has happened. Many hear the teachings, believe, are converted, and are baptized.

l: God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 19
s: God gives Lamoni, the queen, Ammon, and the servants spiritual experiences and power. Ammon prays and gives thanks to God for what has been done for the Lamanites.

l: Lord, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 19
s: The Lord is called upon by the servants and by Abish, and his Spirit is poured out upon the Lamanites. The Lord begins his work among them and extends his arm to all who repent and believe on his name.

l: Christ, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 19
s: The queen cries out to blessed Jesus, saying that he has saved her from an awful hell.

l: Redeemer, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 19
s: Lamoni declares that he has seen his Redeemer and that the Redeemer will come forth, be born of a woman, and redeem all mankind who believe on his name.

l: Great Spirit, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 19
s: Some of the people say that Ammon is the Great Spirit or was sent by the Great Spirit. Others say the Great Spirit sent Ammon to afflict them because of their iniquities and had attended the Nephites.

l: Spirit of the Lord, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 19
s: The Spirit overpowers Lamoni, the queen, and Ammon, causing them to sink to the earth. The servants also fall after the fear of the Lord comes upon them, and the Lord pours out his Spirit upon the Lamanites.

l: the waters of Sebus, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 19
s: The waters of Sebus are where the servants' flocks had been scattered and where Ammon defended the king's flocks. A man whose brother was slain there attacks Ammon with a sword and falls dead.

l: faith in Christ, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 19
s: The queen believes Ammon despite having no witness beyond his word and the servants' word. Ammon tells her that she has exceeding faith, and Mosiah trusts Ammon to the Lord according to his faith.

l: miraculous power of God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 19
s: Abish recognizes that the falling of the king, queen, servants, and Ammon is caused by the power of God. The people also marvel about the great power shown when the attacker falls dead.

l: conversion, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 19
s: Abish had been converted to the Lord for many years. Many of the people are converted to the Lord after hearing the teachings and testimonies of Lamoni, Ammon, and the servants.

l: king Lamoni's awakening, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 19
s: Lamoni awakens on the morrow according to Ammon's words. He rises, praises God, declares that he has seen his Redeemer, and later teaches his people.

l: the servants' falling to the earth, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 19
s: The servants call on the name of the Lord in their might and all fall to the earth except Abish. They later testify that their hearts were changed and that they no longer desired to do evil.

l: the sword attack on Ammon, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 19
s: A man whose brother was slain by Ammon raises a sword to kill Ammon. Before striking him, the man falls dead, and the people fear and marvel.

l: the gathering at the king's house, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 19
s: Abish runs from house to house and makes the events known, causing a multitude to gather at the king's house. The people see the king, queen, servants, and Ammon lying on the earth.

l: baptism, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 19
s: As many of the people believe the words of Lamoni, Ammon, and the servants, they are baptized.

l: establishment of the church, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 19
s: The people who believe and are baptized become a righteous people and establish a church among themselves.

l: the work of the Lord among the Lamanites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 19
s: The work of the Lord commences among the Lamanites as the Lord begins to pour out his Spirit upon them. The account says that his arm is extended to all people who repent and believe on his name.

l: The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 20
s: Ammon is directed by the Lord to go to the land of Middoni to deliver Aaron and his other brethren from prison instead of accompanying Lamoni to the land of Nephi. Lamoni travels with Ammon, defends him before his father, and refuses to kill him or return to the land of Ishmael. Ammon defeats Lamoni’s father in combat and obtains the release of his brethren and the continuation of Lamoni’s rule. In Middoni, Ammon’s brethren are released after suffering hunger, thirst, affliction, beatings, and imprisonment, but remaining patient.

l: Ammon, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 20
s: Ammon is told by the Lord to go to the land of Middoni to deliver his brethren from prison. He protects Lamoni from his father, defeats the king’s attack, and obtains the release of his brethren and the continuation of Lamoni’s rule.

l: Lamoni, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 20
s: Lamoni desires to take Ammon to the land of Nephi to show him to his father, but instead travels with Ammon to the land of Middoni. He refuses his father’s command to slay Ammon and to return to the land of Ishmael, and he retains his kingdom.

l: the king who was Lamoni’s father, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 20
s: The father of Lamoni becomes angry when Lamoni explains that he is going to deliver Ammon’s brethren. He commands Lamoni to slay Ammon, attacks Ammon himself, and then agrees to release Ammon’s brethren and allow Lamoni to retain his kingdom after Ammon overcomes him.

l: Aaron, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 20
s: Aaron is in prison in the land of Middoni with Ammon’s other brethren and is delivered when Lamoni and Ammon arrive.

l: Ammon’s brethren, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 20
s: Ammon’s brethren are imprisoned in Middoni after being rejected, beaten, and driven from place to place. They suffer hunger, thirst, affliction, nakedness, and binding with strong cords, yet remain patient, and are released through Lamoni and Ammon.

l: land of Middoni, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 20
s: The land of Middoni is where Aaron and Ammon’s other brethren are imprisoned. Lamoni and Ammon travel there, and the king of the land favors Lamoni and allows the brethren to be brought out of prison.

l: Lamoni's kingdom, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 20
s: Lamoni’s kingdom is preserved when Ammon requires Lamoni’s father to allow Lamoni to retain it. Lamoni’s father grants that Lamoni may retain the kingdom from that time and forever and will govern him no more.

l: journey to Middoni, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 20
s: Ammon and Lamoni journey toward the land of Middoni after Lamoni prepares horses and chariots. During the journey, they meet the father of Lamoni, and afterward they continue to Middoni.

l: imprisonment of Ammon's brethren, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 20
s: Ammon’s brethren are taken and cast into prison in the land of Middoni, where they are bound with strong cords and kept for many days. Their imprisonment follows their rejection, beatings, and forced movement from house to house and place to place.

l: deliverance of Ammon's brethren, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 20
s: Ammon seeks the deliverance of his brethren from prison in Middoni. Lamoni and Ammon obtain their release, and the brethren are brought forth from prison despite the suffering they endured.

l: The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 21
s: Aaron and his brethren preach the word of God among the Lamanites, Amalekites, and Amulonites in Jerusalem, Ani-Anti, and Middoni, teaching repentance, Christ, the resurrection of the dead, and redemption through his death and sufferings and the atonement of his blood. The Amalekites reject and mock Aaron, and Aaron and some of his brethren are imprisoned in Middoni before Lamoni and Ammon deliver them. The missionaries continue preaching and bring many to a knowledge of the truth, convincing them of their sins and incorrect traditions. In Ishmael, Lamoni establishes religious liberty, builds synagogues, teaches his people, and Ammon exhorts them daily to keep the commandments of God.

l: Ammon, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 21
s: Ammon helps deliver Aaron and the others from prison with Lamoni. He returns with Lamoni to Ishmael, preaches to Lamoni's people, teaches righteousness, and exhorts them daily to keep the commandments of God.

l: Aaron, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 21
s: Aaron travels to Jerusalem and preaches in an Amalekite synagogue about repentance, the coming of Christ, the resurrection of the dead, redemption, and the atonement of Christ's blood. After the people reject him, he preaches in Ani-Anti and Middoni, is imprisoned, is delivered by Lamoni and Ammon, and continues preaching.

l: Lamoni, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 21
s: Lamoni helps deliver Aaron and his brethren from prison and returns with Ammon to Ishmael. He does not allow Ammon to serve him, builds synagogues, teaches his people, and grants them liberty to worship God.

l: Ammon’s brethren, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 21
s: Ammon and his brethren separate in the borders of the land of the Lamanites to preach the word. They suffer rejection, imprisonment, and hardship, but continue preaching and bring many to a knowledge of the truth.

l: Lamanites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 21
s: The Lamanites have built Jerusalem with the Amalekites and the people of Amulon. The Amalekites and Amulonites cause them to harden their hearts and become strong in wickedness, though some Lamanites hear the missionaries' preaching.

l: Amalekites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 21
s: The Amalekites have built Jerusalem and synagogues after the order of the Nehors. An Amalekite contends with Aaron, rejects his teachings, and mocks him when Aaron teaches about Christ.

l: the people of Lamoni, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 21
s: The people of Ishmael are under Lamoni's reign and are taught by Lamoni and Ammon. They are declared free from the oppressions of Lamoni's father and are allowed liberty to worship God, and they heed Ammon's word.

l: Jerusalem, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 21
s: Jerusalem is a great city built by the Lamanites, Amalekites, and people of Amulon. Aaron preaches to the Amalekites in its synagogues.

l: land of Middoni, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 21
s: Middoni is a land where Aaron and his brethren preach after leaving Ani-Anti. Aaron and some of his brethren are taken and cast into prison there, and Lamoni and Ammon deliver them.

l: land of Ishmael, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 21
s: Ishmael is the land of Lamoni's inheritance. Lamoni and Ammon return there, and Lamoni causes synagogues to be built and teaches the people.

l: synagogues, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 21
s: The Amalekites and Amulonites build synagogues after the order of the Nehors, and Aaron preaches in them. Lamoni also causes synagogues to be built in Ishmael.

l: God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 21
s: God is worshiped by the people, and Lamoni teaches that they may worship God according to their desires. Aaron and Ammon teach about God and righteousness.

l: Son of God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 21
s: Aaron asks whether the Amalekite believes that the Son of God shall come to redeem mankind from their sins.

l: Christ, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 21
s: Aaron teaches about the coming of Christ, whose death and sufferings are necessary for the redemption of mankind.

l: word of God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 21
s: The missionaries preach the word of God in synagogues and assemblies wherever they are admitted. Many are convinced by it of their sins and incorrect traditions.

l: repentance, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 21
s: Aaron teaches that people must repent or perish. The Amalekite challenges Aaron's claim that they have cause to repent.

l: resurrection of the dead, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 21
s: Aaron opens the scriptures and teaches the people concerning the resurrection of the dead.

l: redemption of Christ, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 21
s: Aaron teaches that there can be no redemption for mankind except through the death and sufferings of Christ and the atonement of his blood.

l: death and sufferings of Christ, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 21
s: Aaron teaches that the death and sufferings of Christ are required for the redemption of mankind.

l: the Atonement of Christ, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 21
s: Aaron teaches that redemption comes through the atonement of Christ's blood.

l: the tradition of the Lamanites' fathers, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 21
s: The missionaries convince many of their sins and of the traditions of their fathers that were not correct.

l: commandments of God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 21
s: Ammon exhorts Lamoni's people daily to keep the commandments of God, and they give heed to his word.

l: preaching of the word, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 21
s: Aaron, Ammon, and their brethren preach the word in Jerusalem, Ani-Anti, Middoni, and among the Lamanites and Amalekites. They continue preaching after rejection and imprisonment, and the Lord blesses their efforts.

l: imprisonment of Aaron and his brethren, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 21
s: Aaron and a certain number of his brethren are taken and cast into prison in Middoni. They suffer many things before being delivered.

l: deliverance of Ammon's brethren, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 21
s: Lamoni and Ammon deliver Aaron and his brethren from prison, after which they go forth again to declare the word.

l: conversion, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 21
s: The Lord blesses the missionaries so that they bring many to a knowledge of the truth. They convince many of their sins and of the incorrect traditions of their fathers.

l: The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 22
s: Aaron and his brethren go to the palace of the king who was Lamoni’s father and teach him about God, the Great Spirit, repentance, Christ, and the plan of redemption. The king prays to know God, offers to give away his sins, and is struck as if dead, but Aaron raises him and the king and his household are converted unto the Lord. The king pacifies the people, commands Aaron and his brethren to preach, and sends a proclamation throughout the land. The unit also describes the locations and boundaries of the lands of the Lamanites and Nephites, including Bountiful, Desolation, the land northward, and the land southward.

l: Ammon, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 22
s: Ammon continually teaches the people of Lamoni. He remains in the land of Ishmael because the Spirit of the Lord called him there, while Aaron and his brethren go to the land of Nephi.

l: Aaron, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 22
s: Aaron goes with his brethren to the palace of the king who was Lamoni’s father. He teaches the king from the scriptures, explains the plan of redemption, and raises the king from the earth after the king is struck as if dead.

l: Lamoni, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 22
s: Lamoni is the son of the king over the land except the land of Ishmael. His people are continually taught by Ammon.

l: the king who was Lamoni’s father, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 22
s: The king receives Aaron and his brethren and asks about the Spirit of the Lord, repentance, and the words of Ammon. He believes Aaron’s teachings, prays to know God, offers to give away his sins, is struck as if dead, and is raised by Aaron. He ministers to the people, causes his household to be converted, pacifies the multitude, commands Aaron and his brethren to preach, and sends a proclamation throughout the land.

l: the queen, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 22
s: The queen is told that the king has fallen as if dead and commands the servants to slay Aaron and his brethren. When the servants fear, she also fears and commands that the people be called to slay them.

l: Christ, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 22
s: Christ is presented as the one through whom the plan of redemption was prepared. His sufferings and death atone for sins, break the bands of death, and support the hope of glory.

l: God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 22
s: God is taught as the creator of all things in heaven and earth. The king prays for God to make himself known so that he may give away his sins, be raised from the dead, and be saved at the last day.

l: Lord, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 22
s: The Great Spirit is identified with God and is said to have brought the fathers out of the land of Jerusalem and created all things. The king believes that the Great Spirit created all things.

l: the Spirit of the Lord, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 22
s: The Spirit of the Lord calls Ammon to go another way, to the land of Ishmael, to teach the people of Lamoni. The king asks what the Spirit of the Lord is.

l: Aaron and his brethren, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 22
s: Aaron and his brethren go to the land of Nephi and appear before the king who was Lamoni’s father. They teach the king and later preach to the multitude after the king commands them to do so.

l: the servants of the king, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 22
s: The servants see the cause of the king’s fall and refuse to lay their hands on Aaron and his brethren because they fear them. They tell the queen that one of Aaron’s group is mightier than they are and later report the king’s condition to her.

l: the king’s household, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 22
s: The king’s whole household is converted unto the Lord after the king ministers to them.

l: the people of Lamoni, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 22
s: The people of Lamoni are taught continually by Ammon in the land of Ishmael.

l: Lamanites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 22
s: The Lamanites and Nephites are divided by a narrow strip of wilderness. Lamanites live in the wilderness and by the east and west seashores, while the Nephites hem them in on the south and prevent them from possessing the north.

l: Nephites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 22
s: The Nephites possess the northern parts of the land bordering the wilderness and inhabit Bountiful from the east sea to the west sea. With guards and armies, they hem in the Lamanites on the south and prevent them from overrunning the land northward.

l: land of Nephi, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 22
s: Aaron and his brethren are led to the land of Nephi, where the king’s palace is located. The land of Nephi includes wilderness areas where Lamanites live and borders the land of Zarahemla.

l: land of Ishmael, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 22
s: Ammon goes to the land of Ishmael to teach the people of Lamoni. It is excluded from the land ruled by the king who was Lamoni’s father.

l: land of Zarahemla, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 22
s: The land of Zarahemla is separated from the land of Nephi by a narrow strip of wilderness. The Nephites inhabit its northern parts and the land bordering the wilderness.

l: Bountiful, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 22
s: Bountiful is the land southward of the line dividing it from Desolation. The Nephites inhabit it from the east sea to the west sea, and it is a wilderness filled with wild animals.

l: land Desolation, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 22
s: Desolation is the land northward of Bountiful. It reaches the far northern land that had been peopled and destroyed, whose bones had been discovered by the people of Zarahemla.

l: the wilderness, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 22
s: A narrow strip of wilderness divides the land of Zarahemla from the Lamanites and Nephites. The wilderness contains Lamanite settlements and borders the lands on the north and south.

l: land northward, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 22
s: The land northward is separated from the land southward by a small neck of land. It includes Desolation, and the Nephites prevent the Lamanites from overrunning it.

l: the land southward, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 22
s: The land southward is called Bountiful in the area described. It includes the lands of Nephi and Zarahemla and is nearly surrounded by water.

l: holy scriptures, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 22
s: Aaron reads and expounds the scriptures to the king, beginning with the creation of Adam and teaching about commandments, transgression, the fall of man, and redemption.

l: the proclamation, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 22
s: The king sends a proclamation throughout all his land and among the people in the surrounding regions, including areas bordering the seas and wilderness.

l: repentance, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 22
s: Repentance is taught as necessary for salvation and as part of receiving the hope of eternal life. Aaron tells the king to repent of all his sins and call on God in faith.

l: salvation, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 22
s: Ammon’s teaching states that those who repent shall be saved, while those who do not repent shall be cast off at the last day. The king seeks to be saved at the last day.

l: eternal life, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 22
s: The king asks what he must do to receive the eternal life Aaron has taught about. Aaron tells him to bow down before God, repent, and call on God in faith.

l: the creation of Adam, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 22
s: Aaron begins teaching the king from the creation of Adam, explaining how God created man after his own image and gave him commandments.

l: the fall of man, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 22
s: Aaron teaches that because of transgression man had fallen. He explains the fall of man and humanity’s carnal state to the king.

l: the plan of redemption, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 22
s: Aaron teaches that the plan of redemption was prepared from the foundation of the world through Christ for all who believe on his name.

l: the Atonement of Christ, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 22
s: The sufferings and death of Christ are taught to atone for sins through faith and repentance. They also break the bands of death and cause the sting of death to be swallowed up in the hopes of glory.

l: resurrection of the dead, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 22
s: The king asks to be raised from the dead and saved at the last day. Aaron teaches that Christ breaks the bands of death.

l: the last day, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 22
s: Those who do not repent are taught to be cast off at the last day. The king seeks to avoid being cast off and asks to be saved at the last day.

l: conversion, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 22
s: The king’s whole household is converted unto the Lord after he ministers to them.

l: the king’s sins, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 22
s: The king offers to give away all his sins in order to know God and receive salvation. Aaron instructs him to repent of all his sins.

l: death, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 22
s: Aaron teaches that Christ’s death atones for sins and breaks the bands of death. The king is struck as if dead after praying, but Aaron raises him from the earth.

l: The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 23
s: The king of the Lamanites issued a proclamation protecting Ammon, Aaron, Omner, Himni, and their brethren so they could preach the word of God freely throughout the land. Aaron and his brethren established churches and taught the Lamanites, bringing thousands to the knowledge of the Lord, and those who believed did not fall away. The converted Lamanites laid down their weapons of rebellion, became righteous, and took the name Anti-Nephi-Lehies. They became industrious, friendly with the Nephites, and were no longer followed by the curse of God.

l: Ammon, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 23
s: Ammon was protected by the king of the Lamanites from being bound, imprisoned, assaulted, expelled, scourged, or stoned so that he could preach the word of God freely.

l: Aaron, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 23
s: Aaron was protected by the king of the Lamanites and went from city to city establishing churches and teaching the word of God. He also consulted with the king and many priests about the name of the converted people.

l: the king who was Lamoni’s father, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 23
s: The king of the Lamanites was converted unto the Lord along with all his household. He issued a proclamation protecting those who preached the word of God and later consulted with Aaron and the priests about a name for the converted people.

l: Lamanites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 23
s: Thousands of Lamanites were brought to the knowledge of the Lord through preaching and were converted. The converted Lamanites became righteous, laid down their weapons of rebellion, and became friendly with the Nephites, while the Amalekites and Amulonites generally hardened their hearts.

l: Nephites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 23
s: The Nephites were the people whose traditions, records, and prophecies were taught to the converted Lamanites. The Anti-Nephi-Lehies became friendly with them and opened a correspondence.

l: Anti-Nephi-Lehies, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 23
s: The converted people took the name Anti-Nephi-Lehies so they could be distinguished from their brethren and were no longer called Lamanites. They became industrious and friendly with the Nephites.

l: word of God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 23
s: The word of God was to have no obstruction under the king’s proclamation and was preached throughout the land. It was taught by establishing churches and consecrating priests and teachers among the Lamanites.

l: the proclamation, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 23
s: The proclamation ordered the Lamanites not to harm, imprison, expel, or attack Ammon, Aaron, Omner, Himni, or their preaching brethren. It gave them free access to houses, temples, and sanctuaries so they could preach according to their desires.

l: weapons of rebellion, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 23
s: The converted Lamanites laid down the weapons of their rebellion and all their weapons of war. They no longer fought against God or against their brethren.

l: conversion of the king and his people, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 23
s: The king and all his household were converted unto the Lord, and many Lamanites were also converted through preaching, revelation, prophecy, and miracles. Those who believed and were brought to the knowledge of the truth never fell away.

l: preaching of the word, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 23
s: Aaron and his brethren preached and taught the word of God from city to city and from one house of worship to another. Their preaching brought thousands of Lamanites to the knowledge of the Lord and led to great success.

l: burial of weapons of war, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 23
s: The converted Lamanites laid down their weapons of rebellion and stopped fighting against God and their brethren. This change accompanied their becoming a righteous people.

l: The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 24
s: The Amalekites, Amulonites, and unconverted Lamanites stir up anger against the people of Anti-Nephi-Lehi, and the Lamanites prepare to destroy them. Anti-Nephi-Lehi and his people refuse to take up arms, bury their weapons, and covenant with God to give their own lives rather than shed the blood of their brethren. The Lamanites massacre 1,005 people of Anti-Nephi-Lehi, but many Lamanites repent, abandon their weapons, and join the people of God. The unit teaches that those who fall away after enlightenment become more hardened than those who never knew the truth.

l: Amalekites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 24
s: The Amalekites stir up the unconverted Lamanites and Amulonites to anger against their brethren. They form the greatest number of those who slay the people of Anti-Nephi-Lehi, and none of them join the people of the Lord.

l: Amulonites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 24
s: The Amulonites help stir up anger against the people of Anti-Nephi-Lehi. They form the greatest number of those who slay their brethren, and none of them join the people of the Lord.

l: Lamanites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 24
s: The unconverted Lamanites rebel against their king, take up arms, and prepare to destroy the people of Anti-Nephi-Lehi. After killing many of them, many Lamanites repent, throw down their weapons, and join the people of God; those who had fallen away after enlightenment are described as more hardened.

l: people of Anti-Nephi-Lehi, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 24
s: The people of Anti-Nephi-Lehi refuse to take up arms or prepare for war against their brethren. They bury their weapons, covenant to give their own lives rather than shed blood, and 1,005 of them are slain while calling on the name of the Lord.

l: Anti-Nephi-Lehi (king), The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 24
s: Anti-Nephi-Lehi commands his people not to make preparations for war. He teaches them to retain and bury their swords, explaining that God has forgiven them and that they should not stain their swords with the blood of their brethren.

l: Nephites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 24
s: The Nephites come to the people of Anti-Nephi-Lehi and preach to them, convincing them of the traditions of their wicked fathers.

l: Ammon, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 24
s: Ammon and his brethren see the preparations of the Lamanites and come to the land of Midian. They then go to the land of Ishmael to hold a council with Lamoni and Anti-Nephi-Lehi.

l: Anti-Nephi-Lehi (Lamoni's brother), The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 24
s: Anti-Nephi-Lehi meets with Ammon and his brethren and Lamoni in the land of Ishmael to consider how to defend themselves against the Lamanites.

l: God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 24
s: God sends the Nephites to preach to the people of Anti-Nephi-Lehi, gives them a portion of his Spirit, forgives their sins and murders, and removes their guilt. God makes the plan of salvation known and promises salvation to those who die righteous.

l: Son of God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 24
s: The Son of our great God is described as the source through whose merits guilt is taken away and through whose blood stains can be washed bright in the atonement of sins.

l: war against the people of God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 24
s: The Lamanites make preparations for war against the people of God and come to destroy the king and the people of Anti-Nephi-Lehi. The people of Anti-Nephi-Lehi offer no resistance.

l: conversion, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 24
s: Those who are converted unto the Lord will not take up arms against their brethren. Their conversion leads them to refuse war, bury their weapons, and rely on God.

l: repentance, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 24
s: The people of Anti-Nephi-Lehi repent of their sins and murders, and their repentance is described as all they could do to have God take away their stains. Many Lamanites also repent after witnessing the massacre.

l: murder, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 24
s: The people of Anti-Nephi-Lehi are convinced of the many murders they have committed and repent of their sins and murders. Their former acts cause the Lamanites who killed their brethren to be stung and repent.

l: guilt and stains, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 24
s: God takes away the guilt from the hearts of the people of Anti-Nephi-Lehi and removes their stains. Their bright swords become a testimony that they have not stained them again with the blood of their brethren.

l: forgiveness, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 24
s: God forgives the people of Anti-Nephi-Lehi for their many sins and murders through the merits of his Son. This forgiveness leads them to avoid staining their swords again.

l: the Spirit of the Lord, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 24
s: God gives the people a portion of his Spirit, which softens their hearts and helps them open a correspondence with the Nephites.

l: the plan of redemption, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 24
s: God makes the plan of salvation known to the people of Anti-Nephi-Lehi and to future generations through his mercy and visits by angels.

l: the Atonement of Christ, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 24
s: The blood of the Son of our great God is described as being shed for the atonement of the people's sins. The people fear that staining their swords again would prevent them from being washed bright through that blood.

l: mercy, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 24
s: God has mercy on the people of Anti-Nephi-Lehi by making the plan of salvation known and by visiting them through angels. The Lamanites who repent rely upon the mercies of the people whose arms had been lifted to slay them.

l: truth, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 24
s: The Lamanites who are brought to believe and know the truth become firm and are willing to suffer unto death rather than commit sin. More than a thousand are brought to a knowledge of the truth.

l: salvation, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 24
s: The people of Anti-Nephi-Lehi believe that those who are slain while remaining righteous will go to God and be saved. The unit says that the righteous people who were slain have no reason to be doubted as saved.

l: swords, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 24
s: The people of Anti-Nephi-Lehi regard their swords as bright after God removes their stains. They retain and bury the swords so they will remain bright as a testimony that they have not used them again.

l: weapons of war, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 24
s: The people of Anti-Nephi-Lehi bury all weapons used for shedding man's blood. The Lamanites who repent throw down their weapons of war and refuse to take them again.

l: burial of weapons of war, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 24
s: The people of Anti-Nephi-Lehi bury their swords and other weapons deep in the earth. They do this as a testimony to God and men that they will never again use weapons to shed the blood of their brethren.

l: covenant with God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 24
s: The people of Anti-Nephi-Lehi covenant with God that they would give up their own lives rather than shed the blood of their brethren. They also covenant to give to a brother rather than take away and to labor abundantly rather than spend their days in idleness.

l: massacre of the Anti-Nephi-Lehies, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 24
s: The Lamanites slay 1,005 people of Anti-Nephi-Lehi while those people call on the name of the Lord and offer no resistance. The massacre causes many of the Lamanites to feel sorrow, repent, and abandon their weapons.

l: more than a thousand converts, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 24
s: More than a thousand Lamanites are brought to a knowledge of the truth and join the people of God. None of these converts are Amalekites, Amulonites, or of the order of Nehor; they are actual descendants of Laman and Lemuel.

l: enlightenment and apostasy, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 24
s: The unit teaches that people who have been enlightened by the Spirit of God and gained knowledge concerning righteousness, then fall into sin and transgression, become more hardened than if they had never known those things.
